subject: DPA: Backup/DR carve-out + KMS requirement — proposed redlines and eSign plan
messages:
From: Leila Gomez <lgomez@acmetech.com>
To: mina_haddad@redwood.com
Cc: AzureCloudOps <cloudops@acmetech.com>; Thomas Reed <thomas.reed@acmetech.com>
Date: Tue, 25 Aug 2026 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: Redwood DPA — backup/DR carve-out + KMS question

Hi Mina —

Thanks for sending over the DPA draft. Our security team has two outstanding items we need clarity on before legal can sign:

1) Backup/DR copies: we need an explicit carve-out that allows the vendor to retain immutable backups for disaster recovery up to 180 days. We understand this is unusual to include explicitly, but our infra team requires this window for recovery testing.

2) Key management: we require confirmation whether Redwood can support customer-managed keys (BYOK) for encryption-at-rest, or at minimum a KMS integration for dedicated/private deployments. For the hosted API, we'd like to understand how keys are handled and whether a contractual representation can be made.

Also, please send an updated subprocessor list and SOC 2 report (latest). Attached is our DPA checklist; we marked the retention section as high-priority.

Leila
Leila Gomez
Sr. Counsel, Privacy & Security — AcmeTech

Attachments: acme_dpa_checklist.xlsx

From: mina_haddad@redwood.com
To: Leila Gomez <lgomez@acmetech.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com, neha_kapoor@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 25 Aug 2026 12:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Redwood DPA — backup/DR carve-out + KMS question

Leila —

Appreciate the clear ask. Quick responses to the two items and next steps below:

1) Backup/DR retention: Redwood's default retention for backups is 30 days for hosted customers. For enterprise customers on a Dedicated or Private deployment we can contractually allow up to 180 days for immutable backups for DR, provided backups are encrypted and access is logged.

Proposal: Carve-out language allowing immutable backup retention up to 180 days for Dedicated/Private deployments, and a 30-day backup window for hosted SaaS customers. We can add an audit-friendly requirement (access logs + monthly retention attestations).

2) Key management: We support KMS integrations for Redwood Private and Dedicated (customer-provided KMS is supported via our KMS connector). For hosted API customers we do not provide BYOK today, but we can include a contractual representation that keys are managed by Redwood and AES-256 encrypted at rest; we can also offer an SOC 2 addendum and details on key rotation cadence.

I'll loop in Marissa for the redlines and Karthik for a short technical note on the KMS connector. If this proposal is acceptable, we'll produce a marked-up DPA for review and send a DocuSign envelope for execution.

Thanks,
Mina
Mina Haddad
Head of Legal (Contracts) — Redwood Inference

Attachment: request_received_note.txt

From: karthik_iyer@redwood.com
To: mina_haddad@redwood.com, Leila Gomez <lgomez@acmetech.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 26 Aug 2026 08:30:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Redwood DPA — backup/DR carve-out + KMS question

Leila / Mina —

Technical clarifications from infra:

- For Dedicated/Private: we support customer-managed KMS via a connector that integrates with AWS KMS, GCP KMS, and Azure Key Vault. Keys remain under customer control; Redwood holds only encrypted ciphertext. We log all key-access events and can provide access logs on request (subject to the DPA audit clause).

- For Hosted: keys are managed by Redwood; data is encrypted at rest with tenant-separated encryption keys rotated quarterly. We can include a statement of the rotation policy and the threat model.

- Backups: we snapshot object storage and maintain immutable snapshots for DR. For Dedicated/Private we can set retention to 180 days; for hosted we use 30 days by default. If you need hosted customers to have extended backup retention, we can discuss an add-on pricing line.

Happy to jump on a quick 20m call to walk through the connector and logs if Acme's infra team wants.

— Karthik
Principal Infrastructure Engineer — Redwood Inference

From: marissa_cole@redwood.com

Date: Fri, 28 Aug 2026 10:17:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Redwood DPA — backup/DR carve-out + KMS question

Leila —

Attached is a marked-up DPA (Redwood_DPA_v3.2_markedup.pdf) with the suggested language. Summary of the key redlines relevant to your points:

- Section 4.2 (Backups & DR): Added carve-out: "For Dedicated and Private deployments, Vendor may retain immutable DR backups for up to one hundred eighty (180) days solely for disaster recovery and internal restore testing. Such backups shall be encrypted at rest and access to backup media shall be logged and restricted to authorized personnel." We left hosted behavior at 30 days.

- Section 5.1 (Encryption & Keys): Added representation for hosted customers: "Vendor manages encryption keys for the hosted service and uses industry standard AES-256 encryption with quarterly rotation." For Dedicated/Private: "Customer may supply KMS keys via supported connectors; Vendor will not hold plaintext keys."

- Subprocessors: updated list attached (subprocessor-list-2026-08.csv).

Next steps: If this aligns with Acme's needs, we'll prepare the execution package in DocuSign. Proposed signer: Leila (Acme) + Mina (Redwood). Envelope will include the marked PDF and a second rider with the subprocessor list.

Attaching: Redwood_DPA_v3.2_markedup.pdf; subprocessor-list-2026-08.csv

Best,
Marissa Cole
Senior Counsel, Privacy & Partnerships — Redwood Inference

Thanks — the redlines look sensible and the technical clarifications from Karthik address our main concerns. A couple of small asks before we sign:

- For the hosted-key rotation cadence, please add that Redwood will notify customers at least 30 days in advance of any rotation that may materially affect key handling.

If you can accept those two tweaks we can sign. I'll prepare for signature on our side pending the changes.

Leila
